cards.power: The Great Reset. Forces all players to discard their 'Property' cards.
cards.lore: You will own nothing. The 2030 Agenda isn't a prediction; it's a schedule.
cards.gradeReason: Spider-tycoon weaving the globe — embodiment complete before you read the card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: pulp conspiracy comic. Subject: fat spider in top hat weaving neon web over globe. Mood: sinister omnipotence.

cards.power: Common Core Injection. Pay 2 Billion to standardize all opponent hands.
cards.lore: Funding the control grid, one grant at a time. The revolution will be funded.
cards.gradeReason: Vampire bat with FUNDING syringe — villain archetype zero explanation needed.

cards.power: Standardize the Soul. Nullifies any 'Critical Thinking' cards in play.

cards.gradeReason: Oil-dripping skeleton eagle with 'General Education Board' scroll — haunting and instantly played.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: vintage dark editorial. Subject: oil-soaked skeleton eagle clutching education charter scroll. Mood: industrial-age dread.

cards.power: The Doorway. Opens the path for all other 'Programming' cards to enter the game.

cards.gradeReason: Beaver stacking COMPLIANCE alphabet blocks — builder of obedience systems, immediately embody-able.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: propaganda cartoon. Subject: industrious beaver stacking ABC blocks spelling COMPLIANCE beside engineering plans. Mood: cheerful menace.

cards.power: Meta-Extraction. Steal 1 "Secret" from every player.
cards.lore: Connecting the world to the database. $3.3 million invested to map your child's heart.
cards.gradeReason: Cyborg chameleon with drones in classroom — information predator, play it and steal immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tech-horror comic. Subject: mechanical chameleon camouflaged as teacher, drones tagged Privacy buzzing in classroom. Mood: unseen extraction.

cards.power: Human Capital Futures. Gain $11 for every $1 spent on "Programming" cards.

cards.gradeReason: Shark in pinstripe suit with calculator — profit-from-children archetype, instant table impact.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Wall Street satire. Subject: great white shark in business suit brandishing calculator showing 11:1. Mood: predatory ROI.

cards.power: The Blueprint. View top 3 cards of the deck and rearrange them.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: corporate noir. Subject: hyena in suit presenting glowing Digital ID blueprint. Mood: gleeful architecture of control.

cards.power: Neurophilosophy. Force an opponent to reroll their "Free Will" check.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: occult academic. Subject: glowing owl reading Spirituality book radiating brain-wave energy. Mood: hidden metaphysical control.

cards.power: Trojan Horse. This card cannot be blocked. It enters play disguised as a "Health" card.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: children's book horror. Subject: cute colorful worm infiltrating red apple labeled Health. Mood: innocent corruption.

cards.power: Cradle to Grave. Attach this card to a "Student" card to control them for the rest of the game.

cards.gradeReason: Stitched teddy bear getting electrocuted by gloved hands — cradle-to-grave control made viscerally visible.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: medical horror comic. Subject: patched teddy bear wired to electrodes, blue-gloved hands controlling. Mood: institutional possession.

cards.power: Grit Training. The target must endure damage without complaining.

cards.gradeReason: Donkey crushed under TRAUMA safe — clear visual but the concept needs that 'obedience under pressure' line explained.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark fable. Subject: exhausted donkey crushed beneath heavy safe labeled TRAUMA, grinning through pain. Mood: weaponized endurance.

cards.power: Outcome Equalizer. All players must discard down to the lowest hand size.

cards.gradeReason: Robot with axe equalizing giraffe and elephant — forced sameness made horrifying and instantly understood.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: political cartoon. Subject: robotic figure using industrial axe to shorten giraffe to elephant height, bureaucratic scale behind. Mood: coerced equality.

cards.power: Batch Process. Convert 3 "Individual" tokens into "Worker" tokens.

cards.gradeReason: Pigs on factory conveyor belt becoming grey boxes — most efficient argument against compulsory schooling ever made.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: industrial satire. Subject: assembly line converting squealing piglets into identical grey concrete blocks. Mood: industrial soul erasure.

cards.power: Psychographic Profiling. Look at an opponent's hand and name their insecurities.
cards.lore: How do you feel today? The algorithm needs to know. Aggregating "feelings" for the state database.
cards.gradeReason: Mole with GoPro helmet rifling through child's diary — surveillance of inner life made tangible and immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surveillance thriller. Subject: armored mole with GoPro helmet excavating diaries labeled My Secrets. Mood: interior invasion.

cards.power: Early Intervention. Remove a 'Parent' card from play to 'support' the child.
cards.lore: Separating the child from the family unit. Diagnosing normal childhood as a disorder.
cards.gradeReason: Wolf in nurse outfit with butterfly net labeled Mental Health Checklist — villain of the decade in one image.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: noir institutional horror. Subject: wolf in nurse uniform with butterfly net and mental health checklist, hunting. Mood: predatory benevolence.

cards.power: Timeline Acceleration. Skip the opponent's next turn.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dystopian bureaucracy. Subject: UN-branded pigeon beside clock face filled with ZERO HOUR labels, gears turning. Mood: engineered urgency.

cards.power: Haptic Feedback. Force a player to change their last action.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: biopunk horror. Subject: snake with screen face coiling tightly around human wrist, eye watching. Mood: biometric leash.

cards.power: Metaverse Exile. Place a player in "Time Out" for 2 turns.

cards.gradeReason: Ostrich with TV-helmet burying head in metaverse while real world burns — zero explanation required.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: tech satire. Subject: ostrich wearing boxy VR headset, head down, while wildfire engulfs background. Mood: blissful ignorance.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: surveillance tech horror. Subject: giant camera lens with human eye aperture trained on panicked rabbit. Mood: panoptic capture.

cards.power: Access Denied. Block a player from using "Cash" or "Travel" cards.

cards.power: Social Credit. If your score drops below 0, you lose the game immediately.

cards.power: Cancel Culture. Target player cannot speak for one round.

verdict: FrizzleBob says: This deck is a siege weapon disguised as a card game. Sixty cards, each naming real organizations and real programs, each with a mechanic that mirrors the actual control structure it's lampooning. The villain faction (Weaver, Philanthro-Vampire, Counselor, Emotion Police) is one of the strongest antagonist rosters in the whole corpus — every single character is immediately embody-able. The hero cards (Homeschooler, Non-Complier, Glitch, Saboteur) hit like a catharsis burst in the back half. One urgent fix: The Biometric Scanner card (card 19) has no power/lore text visible in the PDF — probable layout defect. Three minor typos spotted (Schoel for School p.3, sachange for exchange p.11, Kow weeks the curve p.14). Table-ready: YES, but fix that scanner card first.
blurb: For anyone suspicious of what's really being taught in schools — 60 cards exposing the SEL industry, data-mining apparatus, and global curriculum machine, with enough dark humor to survive the rabbit hole.

coverQA.coverNote: No cover page, detective — this deck goes straight to the evidence board, no preamble. Bold commitment to the conspiracy-dossier aesthetic, but you are losing a shareable hook. The first page works as a statement of intent (Weaver plus Philanthro-Vampire opening 1-2 punch is strong), just not designed as a cover.

notes: Deck runs 15 pages x 4 cards = 60 cards, all standard 2x2 grid layout. RAF dice boxes present on all cards; page 7 shows numerical RAF values for The Dept of Ed (R4/A5/F6), The Mandate (R2/A3/F5), USAID (R3/A4/F2), The Census (R1/A2/F4) — rest have empty boxes. Card 19 (The Biometric Scanner) has no visible power/lore text in this PDF rendering — appears to be a layout defect where the card image is full-bleed with no text area. Three visible typos: Schoel for School (The Whole Child p.3); sachange for exchange (The World Bank p.11); Kow weeks the curve marginal annotation on p.14. Deck structure: villain bosses (Weaver/Philanthro-Vampire/Oil Baron Ghost/Social Engineer/Data Merchant/ROI Shark), mechanism cards (SEL/Whole Child/Obedience School as enablers), surveillance apparatus (Data Miner/Biometric Scanner/Census/Scorekeeper), globalist organizations (UNESCO/World Bank/OECD/USAID), and resistance/hero faction (Homeschooler/Non-Complier/Cash Is King/Glitch/Saboteur/FrizzleBob). COVID page (p.14) integrates cleanly as a deployment-event subset. Uncle FrizzleBob wildcard closes the deck as signature. No cover page — deck jumps straight into cards.

marketingText:
Kayfabizarro: PROGRAMMING THE WHOLE CHILD – The Education-Control Apparatus, Dealt Face-Up (Free Cut & Play Comic Card Game)

Who decided your kid's feelings were a revenue stream?

Here is the machine, running in daylight. It enters as Social-Emotional Learning, the one program a parent cannot object to without sounding like a monster, and once it is inside the classroom it quietly stops measuring math and starts measuring the child: mood, compliance, "grit," the shape of a personality logged before that personality has finished forming. The "Whole Child" is the pitch. The whole dataset is the deliverable. The Heckman Equation bolts a dollar sign onto a five-year-old and files it under return on investment.
